note: Independently re-judged 2026-10-28 after the ba03d7c2c7 ESP cipher change, from rfc/full/rfc5282.txt Section 8: "This document further updates [RFC4306] to require that if all of the encryption algorithms in any proposal are authenticated encryption algorithms, then the proposal MUST NOT propose any integrity transforms." Read all four tagged units and the test wrappers forwarding to wireIKEOffer and espProposalWire. The IKE and ESP positives each offer one AES-GCM cipher while retaining a configured SHA256 hash, so an incorrect unconditional integrity emitter has a real transform to emit. Each asserts exactly zero Type 3 transforms, not merely AUTH_NONE: an explicit NONE transform would fail. The IKE positive additionally requires ENCR, PRF and DH; the ESP positive requires ENCR and ESN, so an empty or truncated proposal cannot satisfy absence vacuously. The separate AES-CBC controls require exactly one Type 3 on each rail, testing the boundary of the AEAD condition rather than permitting unconditional omission. The native builders currently emit one encryption transform per proposal, so 'all' is the sole cipher, not an untested multi-cipher conjunction within a proposal. wireIKEOffer guards the integrity append with !enc.IsAEAD; the changed espProposalWire still guards it with !p.Encryption.IsAEAD(), now looking up non-AEAD integrity through lookupESPIntegrity. Reading the property and registry producers confirms AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 are AEAD while NULL and 3DES are not; the new ESP-only hash lookup does not move the append outside that guard. Retain enforced for proposal construction on both IKE and ESP rails. The tagged executions are AES-GCM/AES-CBC examples, not a runtime enumeration of every cipher or a packet-capture proof. Existing revert records show dependency on the builders, not independent proof of every conditional; new native record observations are a separate deliverable. No tests were run by this auditor.
